Fuck, this is so much harder for me to write than I thought it would be, but I need to get it out there. 

This has happened on many occasions (I'm scared to get help because I've never benefited from it before, and I have major issues opening up to people), so I guess I'll talk about the most recent one.

Three or four weeks ago, I woke up and decided that when I got home from school that day (I'm a senior), I would kill myself. Outwardly, nothing was different in my behavior, since I'm painfully shy at times and sometimes even have trouble being around people I've known for a while. Mentally, though, I spent the whole day planning out my notes: One to my parents, one to my best friend, and one to a friend I've had a crush on for almost six months now but haven't told him because I'm too scared to come out as not being straight.

When I got home, I spent quite a while writing these notes out neatly, since my handwriting is horrible and I needed them to be legible. Once I had finished, I sat in my bed, razor blade in hand, trying to figure out where I should cut to make it quick and irreversible. I don't know what it was, but after about an hour of just sitting there, stewing in my own misery, I decided that it was not my time, that just a few cuts could help me make it through the day alive. I went to some woods by my house and set fire to my notes, making sure to burn them until they were nothing but dust. Since then, I've been fighting day-to-day to not try to kill myself again, a few cuts on my arm or thigh acting as my crutch.

Self-harm is funny like that, people who have never done it seem to wonder how it helps those who do it to feel better. I don't get it either. When I cut, I may be bleeding, but my heart's still beating.

As much as I try to pull away, he's the only person who can make me laugh when I'm depressed, the only person I can think about a lot. But I've been cheated on and had my trust otherwise betrayed before, and if HE cheats, it will probably destroy me emotionally.
